key_insight: A PINN built on the Savage-Hutter model can learn avalanche height and velocity in 1D and, with sparse experimental data, generalize to realistic 2D granular collapse dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-guided tool for avalanche hazard prediction that can reduce dependence on dense measurements while still matching key runout and deposit patterns.
method: Verified three 1D cases against analytical solutions: prescribed-velocity height prediction, prescribed-height velocity prediction, and coupled conservative-form training.
Extended to 2D cylindrical pile collapse on an incline and trained a hybrid PINN with 10 sparse final-deposit points after pure physics training collapsed to the trivial zero solution.
Compared predictions with laboratory experiments and TITAN2D using RMSE, peak flow depth/velocity, and wetted-area IoU.
evidence_signal: In 2D validation across four experimental cases, global height RMSE was 2.7–6.7 mm and mean wetted-area IoU was 69–81%, while the coupled 1D test achieved height/velocity RMSEs of 0.043 and 0.079.
watch_item: Pure physics-only training failed by converging to the zero solution, so the approach still depends on sparse observational data and careful loss balancing.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Depth-Averaged Avalanche Dynamics
